R-performance-1 (One customer query per invoice in the monthly report) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: N+1 queries: `customer_label` calls `db.customer(invoice.customer_id)` (src/report.rs:39, `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1`) once per invoice, so a month of about 3 000 invoices from 800 customers runs about 3 000 customer queries plus the list query, and the count grows linearly with the month's invoices. Collect the distinct `customer_id`s, load them with the existing batch method `db.customers(&ids)` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`), index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>` and build each label from the map — two queries per report whatever the volume. Keep the invoice-number order and return the same error when a customer is missing.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

    let pattern = Regex::new(r"PO-\d{4}-\d{4}").expect("a valid pattern");
findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for every invoice of the loop (src/report.rs:28) and calls `Regex::new` each time, so a report of about 3 000 invoices compiles the same pattern about 3 000 times — compile cost that grows with the month's invoices and dwarfs the per-note match. Compile it once: a `static PO_PATTERN: std::sync::LazyLock<Regex>` (or `once_cell::sync::Lazy`), or build it in `monthly_report` before the loop and pass it in. The matching behavior stays the same.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled once per invoice
